hints: At constant speed, the power supplied to overcome a resistive force depends on the force and the speed along its direction.
Use P = Fv with F = 18 N and v = 1.4 m s⁻¹.
walkthrough: The trolley moves at constant speed, so the supplied power must balance the energy transferred each second against the 18 N resistive force.
Use mechanical power P = Fv.
To two significant figures, the required power is 25 W.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses mechanical power as force multiplied by speed.
Calculates 18 N × 1.4 m s⁻¹ and gives 25 W, or the unrounded value 25.2 W.

hints: After release, the 18 N resistive force is the resultant force and acts opposite to the trolley's motion.
First find the magnitude of the deceleration from F = ma; then use the change from 1.4 m s⁻¹ to rest to find the time.
walkthrough: Once released, the only horizontal resultant force is the 18 N resistive force, so its acceleration is opposite to the initial motion.
Its magnitude is a = F / m = 18 N / 72 kg = 0.25 m s⁻².
The speed decreases from 1.4 m s⁻¹ to 0, so using magnitude values, time = change in speed / deceleration = 1.4 / 0.25 = 5.6 s.
Therefore, the trolley takes 5.6 s to come to rest.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the resultant resistive force and trolley mass to set a = F / m.
Obtains a deceleration magnitude of 0.25 m s⁻² and relates the 1.4 m s⁻¹ speed decrease to the stopping time.
Gives a stopping time of 5.6 s.

hints: Along the slope, the weight component pulls the trolley downhill while the resistive force acts uphill.
Find the resultant force and acceleration first, then apply the constant-acceleration relationship for a trolley starting from rest over 9.5 m.
walkthrough: Taking downhill as positive, the resultant force is 54 N − 18 N = 36 N downhill.
Use F = ma: a = 36 N / 72 kg = 0.50 m s⁻².
The trolley starts from rest and travels 9.5 m with constant acceleration, so v² = u² + 2as = 0 + 2(0.50)(9.5) = 9.5 m² s⁻².
v = √9.5 = 3.08 m s⁻¹, so the speed at Y is 3.1 m s⁻¹.

ai_rubric.observable: Finds the 36 N downhill resultant force and obtains an acceleration of 0.50 m s⁻² using the 72 kg mass.
Uses the constant-acceleration relationship with u = 0, a = 0.50 m s⁻² and s = 9.5 m.
Gives a speed of 3.1 m s⁻¹, or the unrounded value about 3.08 m s⁻¹.

hints: The given force F acts along the trolley's movement down the slope, so use the force component in the direction of the 9.5 m displacement.
Apply W = Fs with F = 54 N and s = 9.5 m.
walkthrough: Work done by a constant force is W = Fs when the force acts in the direction of the displacement.
The 54 N component F is along the slope, as is the 9.5 m movement from X to Y.
To two significant figures, the work done is 510 J.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates 54 N × 9.5 m and gives 510 J, or the unrounded value 513 J.

hints: Work done by F increases as the trolley moves farther down the slope, and it is zero before any distance has been travelled.
The trolley starts from rest and accelerates at a constant rate, so distance travelled in each further second becomes larger. Use this to decide how the graph's gradient changes.
walkthrough: The force F is constant and acts along the slope, so W = Fs: work done is proportional to the distance travelled.
At t = 0, the trolley is at X and its displacement is zero, so the graph starts at the origin.
The trolley starts from rest with constant acceleration, so s = ½at². Hence W is proportional to t² rather than t.
Sketch a rising curved line from the origin that becomes progressively steeper; its gradient increases with time.

ai_rubric.observable: Draws a rising curved line starting at the origin.
Shows that the graph gradient increases with time, giving an upward-curving shape.

hints: The stated frictional forces at the wheels may be constant, but they are not the only force resisting the trolley's motion.
Consider what happens to air resistance as the trolley's speed changes while it travels down the slope.
walkthrough: As the trolley accelerates down the slope, its speed increases.
Air resistance depends on speed, so it increases as the trolley moves faster.
Although the wheel friction is constant, the air-resistance contribution changes; therefore the total resistive force is not constant.

ai_rubric.observable: Explains that air resistance changes, specifically increasing with the trolley's speed, so the total resistive force cannot remain constant.
